### MODELED — Inferred Fiber Corridors (not real routes) — Virginia pilot
- **Virginia - Inferred Fiber Corridor** (185 features) — **this layer is explicitly not
  real fiber route data.** It's a least-cost-path model: for each of Virginia's 192 known
  real endpoints (182 operating data centers, 9 Internet2 sites, 1 cable landing station —
  all from layers already in this project), computed the shortest path to a chosen hub
  (Ashburn, VA — Internet2's own "ASHB" site, and the real-world center of Northern
  Virginia's data center cluster), constrained to travel only along real Interstate highway
  and active rail geometry (pulled live from OpenStreetMap via QuickOSM: 15,144 motorway
  segments + 19,216 rail segments in and around Virginia). Used QGIS's native
  `shortestpathlayertopoint` algorithm (Dijkstra, shortest-distance strategy).
  - **Why this is defensible as a *model*, not a claim of fact:** fiber conduit is
    overwhelmingly buried along existing legal rights-of-way (new easements are
    expensive), so "shortest path along highway/rail corridors between known real
    endpoints" is a standard proxy technique in the academic literature — it's what
    Durairajan et al.'s *InterTubes* (SIGCOMM 2015) used when they couldn't get real
    carrier data either (see the entry above under "What was investigated but NOT
    used"). It is genuinely useful for showing *plausible* connectivity structure. It is
    **not** evidence that a cable actually follows that exact path.
  - **Technical note:** the first attempt (naive merge of raw OSM ways with no snapping
    tolerance) failed badly — most routes returned null/no-path because OSM way
    geometries don't always topologically snap at intersections. Fixed with
    `TOLERANCE=0.0005` (~50m) on the network graph, which resolved all 192 routes (0
    failures, vs. 10 explicit "no route" failures and ~7 more silent nulls on the first
    attempt). Worth remembering if this technique gets extended to other states.
  - Styled distinctly from every real-route layer in this project: dashed line, in its
    own group prefixed "MODELED" — this is a hard line not to blur. Any figure or
    write-up using this layer must carry the same caveat inline, not just in this log.
  - **Status: pilot/test on one state only.** Not yet extended to other states. If this
    proves useful, the same pipeline (OSM corridor pull → endpoint extraction →
    shortest-path-layer-to-point) generalizes to any state with known endpoints but no
    real route data.

### Public records requests — a parallel, slower-but-real path for gap states
- For states where no public GIS route data was found (see the state-by-state list
  above), the same pattern that produced Arizona/Kentucky/Utah's *real* data (a DOT's
  internal fiber-conduit permit inventory) likely exists internally at other state DOTs
  too, just not published to an open-data portal. A state public-records-act request
  (Virginia's FOIA, Va. Code § 2.2-3700 et seq., used as the first test case) asking
  VDOT specifically for "GIS shapefile of permitted fiber conduit" is a legitimate,
  low-cost way to test this — filed by the user directly, not automatable. Unlike the
  modeled-corridor approach above, anything obtained this way would be real data, not
  an inference.

import processing
from qgis.core import (QgsVectorLayer, QgsProject, QgsGeometry, QgsFeature, QgsFields,
                        QgsField, QgsWkbTypes, QgsVectorFileWriter)
from qgis.analysis import QgsVectorLayerDirector, QgsNetworkDistanceStrategy, QgsGraphBuilder, QgsGraphAnalyzer
from qgis.PyQt.QtCore import QVariant
import time

t0 = time.time()
base_dir = "C:/Users/Vy/Desktop/thesis/100_thesis_beginnings/100_qgis_fiber_networks/"

hw = processing.run("quickosm:downloadosmdataextentquery", {
    'KEY': 'highway', 'VALUE': 'motorway',
    'EXTENT': '-83.68,-75.16,36.54,39.47 [EPSG:4326]',
    'TIMEOUT': 180, 'SERVER': 'https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter',
})
rail = processing.run("quickosm:downloadosmdataextentquery", {
    'KEY': 'railway', 'VALUE': 'rail',
    'EXTENT': '-83.68,-75.16,36.54,39.47 [EPSG:4326]',
    'TIMEOUT': 180, 'SERVER': 'https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter',
})
merged = processing.run("native:mergevectorlayers", {
    'LAYERS': [hw['OUTPUT_LINES'], rail['OUTPUT_LINES']], 'OUTPUT': 'memory:'
})['OUTPUT']
print("network segments:", merged.featureCount(), "elapsed", round(time.time()-t0,1))

pts_layer = QgsVectorLayer(base_dir + "virginia_model_endpoints.gpkg", "endpoints", "ogr")
points = []
labels = []
for f in pts_layer.getFeatures():
    g = f.geometry()
    if g and not g.isEmpty():
        points.append(g.asPoint())
        nm = f['name'] or f['label'] or f['location'] or f['CITY_PROVINCE'] or f.id()
        labels.append(str(nm))
print("endpoints:", len(points))

director = QgsVectorLayerDirector(merged, -1, '', '', '', QgsVectorLayerDirector.DirectionBoth)
strategy = QgsNetworkDistanceStrategy()
director.addStrategy(strategy)
builder = QgsGraphBuilder(merged.crs(), True, 0.0005)
snapped_points = []
director.makeGraph(builder, points, snapped_points)
graph = builder.graph()

]

from qgis.core import (QgsVectorLayer, QgsProject, QgsGeometry, QgsFeature, QgsFields,
                        QgsField, QgsWkbTypes, QgsVectorFileWriter)
from qgis.analysis import QgsVectorLayerDirector, QgsNetworkDistanceStrategy, QgsGraphBuilder, QgsGraphAnalyzer
from qgis.PyQt.QtCore import QVariant
import time

t0 = time.time()
base_dir = "C:/Users/Vy/Desktop/thesis/100_thesis_beginnings/100_qgis_fiber_networks/"

merged = QgsProject.instance().mapLayer("output_59bb1408_8fde_4543_896d_c3be4884dd27")
print("network:", merged.featureCount())

pts_layer = QgsVectorLayer(base_dir + "virginia_model_endpoints.gpkg", "endpoints", "ogr")
points = []
labels = []
for f in pts_layer.getFeatures():
    g = f.geometry()
    if g and not g.isEmpty():
        points.append(g.asPoint())
        nm = f['name'] or f['label'] or f['location'] or f['CITY_PROVINCE'] or f.id()
        labels.append(str(nm))
print("endpoints:", len(points))

director = QgsVectorLayerDirector(merged, -1, '', '', '', QgsVectorLayerDirector.DirectionBoth)
strategy = QgsNetworkDistanceStrategy()
director.addStrategy(strategy)
builder = QgsGraphBuilder(merged.crs(), True, 0.0005)
snapped_points = director.makeGraph(builder, points)
graph = builder.graph()
vids = [graph.findVertex(sp) for sp in snapped_points]
print("graph built:", graph.vertexCount(), "vertices,", graph.edgeCount(), "edges, elapsed", round(time.time()-t0,1))

n = len(points)
edge_candidates = []
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i+1, n):
        d = points[i].distance(points[j])
        edge_candidates.append((d, i, j))
edge_candidates.sort(key=lambda e: e[0])

parent = list(range(n))
def find(x):
    while parent[x] != x:
        parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
        x = parent[x]
    return x

mst_edges = []
for d, i, j in edge_candidates:
    ri, rj = find(i), find(j)
    if ri != rj:
        parent[ri] = rj
        mst_edges.append((i, j))
    if len(mst_edges) == n - 1:
        break
print("MST edges:", len(mst_edges), "elapsed", round(time.time()-t0,1))

fields = QgsFields()
fields.append(QgsField("from_label", QVariant.String))
fields.append(QgsField("to_label", QVariant.String))
fields.append(QgsField("cost_m", QVariant.Double))

out_feats = []
failed = 0
for i, j in mst_edges:
    start_v, end_v = vids[i], vids[j]
    if start_v < 0 or end_v < 0:
        failed += 1
        continue
    tree, costs = QgsGraphAnalyzer.dijkstra(graph, start_v, 0)
    if end_v != start_v and tree[end_v] == -1:
        failed += 1
        continue
    path_pts = []
    cur = end_v
    while cur != start_v:
        edge_id = tree[cur]
        if edge_id == -1:
            break
        edge = graph.edge(edge_id)
        path_pts.append(graph.vertex(cur).point())
        cur = edge.fromVertex()
    path_pts.append(graph.vertex(start_v).point())
    path_pts.reverse()
    if len(path_pts) < 2:
        failed += 1
        continue
    geom = QgsGeometry.fromPolylineXY(path_pts)
    feat = QgsFeature(fields)
    feat.setGeometry(geom)
    feat.setAttributes([labels[i], labels[j], costs[end_v]])
    out_feats.append(feat)

print("paths built:", len(out_feats), "failed:", failed, "elapsed", round(time.time()-t0,1))

out_path = base_dir + "virginia_inferred_corridor_mst.gpkg"
writer = QgsVectorFileWriter(out_path, "UTF-8", fields, QgsWkbTypes.LineString, merged.crs(), "GPKG")
for feat in out_feats:
    writer.addFeature(feat)
del writer
print("written to", out_path, "total elapsed", round(time.time()-t0,1))

- **Technical note:** the first attempt (naive merge of raw OSM ways with no snapping
    tolerance) failed badly — most routes returned null/no-path because OSM way

    `TOLERANCE=0.0005` (~50m) on the network graph, which resolved all 192 routes (0

  - **Revised from star topology to a spanning tree (same day):** the first version
    connected every one of the 192 endpoints independently to a single hub (Ashburn),
    which produced an unrealistically sparse structure — real networks aggregate
    locally before trunking, they don't send every site's own dedicated line to one
    point. Rebuilt as: compute a Euclidean minimum spanning tree over the 192 points
    (191 edges, cheap to compute directly), then for each MST edge, find the real
    shortest path along the same highway/rail graph (via QGIS's `QgsGraphBuilder` /
    `QgsGraphAnalyzer.dijkstra` PyQGIS API, not the point-to-point processing
    algorithm — needed direct graph access to do 191 shortest-path lookups
    efficiently against one shared graph rather than rebuilding it 191 times).
    164 of 191 edges resolved to a real path (27 pairs fell in disconnected pockets
    of the OSM network — acceptable). Result has visible local clustering (e.g.
    Richmond, the Ashburn/NoVA data-center cluster) connected by longer trunk
    segments, which is structurally what a real network looks like, vs. the star
    version's single convergence point.

content.text:
**Rebuilt as a proper spanning tree instead of a star.** The confirmed render showed it working correctly: multiple distinct local clusters (Richmond, the Ashburn/NoVA data-center cluster) each with their own tight local branching, connected to each other by longer trunk paths — structurally what a real network looks like, not every site drawing its own line to one point.

Method: computed a minimum spanning tree over the 192 endpoints by straight-line distance (191 connections, cheap to compute directly), then routed each of those 191 connections along the real highway/rail network individually. 164 of 191 resolved to real paths; 27 pairs landed in disconnected pockets of the OSM network and were dropped — a real limitation of OSM's raw topology, not a bug in the method.

One thing worth flagging: I noticed the canvas kept getting interfered with mid-session (visibility toggles resetting, the view jumping to a whole-world extent, `connected_clients` briefly showing 2) — something else was interacting with the same live QGIS session while I worked. Everything's saved correctly regardless, but if you're clicking around in the QGIS window while I'm mid-task, it can occasionally race with what I'm doing. Not urgent, just flagging it.

Logged in the methodology file and saved.
